subject.title: Windows QuickStart defaults first chat to paid Anthropic model without credit warning

question: What first-run Anthropic policy should Windows QuickStart use before Terminal hatch when the selected/default model may require paid credits?
rationale: The source proves the current warning is missing, but changing defaults or gating Terminal hatch changes provider setup policy and first-run UX.

options.title: Warn and offer recovery before hatch
options.body: Keep explicit Anthropic selection but show paid-credit readiness, then offer model/provider switch, billing setup, or intentional continue before launching Terminal chat.

options.title: Change the first-run default model
options.body: Move QuickStart Anthropic setup to a lower-cost or beta-safe default, with upgrade/default preservation tests for existing users.

options.title: Document intentional Opus behavior
options.body: Leave the default unchanged and document the billing requirement, accepting that unsupported first-run accounts can still fail after setup.

recommendation.title: Warn and offer recovery before hatch
recommendation.body: Keep explicit Anthropic selection but show paid-credit readiness, then offer model/provider switch, billing setup, or intentional continue before launching Terminal chat.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history points to the Anthropic default policy and setup wizard surfaces introduced by steipete-authored commits.
